name: Difference of Sex Development

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Statement on Management of Intersex Disorders

criteria.description: Presence of ambiguous or atypical external genitalia at birth
Discordance between chromosomal sex and gonadal or phenotypic sex
Abnormal serum levels of sex steroids or their precursors
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with sex development

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia or discordant chromosomal and phenotypic sex with supportive biochemical or genetic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including endocrinology, genetics, and urology.

pathognomonic.notes: Variable degrees of genital ambiguity including hypospadias, clitoromegaly, or micropenis
Karyotype does not match external genital phenotype
searchTerms: mismatch between chromosomes and physical sex

common.notes: Incomplete or abnormal development of testes or ovaries
Urethral opening located on the ventral side of the penis
Failure to develop secondary sexual characteristics

occasional.notes: Absence of menstruation by age 15 in phenotypic females
Breast tissue development in phenotypic males
Impaired fertility due to gonadal dysfunction
May be associated with some DSD syndromes

rare.notes: Life-threatening adrenal insufficiency in congenital adrenal hyperplasia variants

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric distress related to gender identity
rare.notes: Psychosocial challenges due to discordant sex characteristics
Increased risk of gonadoblastoma or dysgerminoma

laboratory: Abnormal serum sex steroid hormone levels (e.g., testosterone, estradiol, 17-hydroxyprogesterone)
Elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in gonadal dysgenesis
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing presence or absence of uterus and gonads
MRI for detailed gonadal and internal reproductive anatomy
genetic: Karyotyping revealing sex chromosome anomalies (e.g., 46,XY; 46,XX; mosaicism)
Molecular genetic testing identifying mutations in genes such as SRY, NR5A1, AR, SOX9
other: Histopathological examination of gonadal tissue if biopsy performed

distinguishingFeatures: Normal to elevated testosterone levels with end-organ resistance

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth requiring urgent evaluation
Salt-wasting crisis or adrenal insufficiency symptoms
Rapid onset of virilization or feminization during infancy or puberty
references: Hughes IA, Houk C, Ahmed SF, Lee PA. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006;91(7):554-563.
